title: Milk Production Systems: Lactation Biology, Yield Optimization, and Efficiency Control in Modern Dairy Herds
excerpt: Milk production is the final biological expression of genetics, nutrition, health, and management acting in synchrony. Modern dairy systems no longer view milk yield as a simple outcome of feeding and milking, but as a tightly regulated physiological process governed by endocrine control, mammary cell dynamics, metabolic balance, and environmental stability. This chapter presents a PhD-grade, systems-level exploration of lactation biology, milk synthesis mechanisms, production curves, and management strategies required to sustainably optimize yield, efficiency, and milk quality.
